approach: I followed the FE-02 procedure in the frontend-steps skill. First I read feat.tasks to find the Frontend task: TSK-07 in ap_portal, which renders HTML from given rows, uses no transport layer and touches only the files in its budget. The permission table is restricted, so I used the tool view's summary of it. Shell commands are blocked for FE-02, so I checked the ap_portal checkout with Glob, Grep and Read. I read src/ap_portal/index.js, package.json, ci.mjs and tests/portal.test.js in full to look for secret, token or environment use, dependencies and network calls. The task needs no secret and the permission table grants none, so there is no gap and I raised no access request. I wrote task.secrets_scope with secret names only, which here means none.

improvements: Section 4 says FE-02 'must run again, because that would be a re-entry trigger' if a network call, registry-token dependency or deployed environment is added. No source defines the re-entry triggers (footnote ¹ in the workbook is not expanded anywhere the agent read). Label this as agent judgement, or point it to whoever owns the trigger list.

Section 4 does not say who an access request would go to, or through which channel (for example capability_request to the owner of org.permission_table), if a secret is needed later. Naming both would make the 'ask for access as needed' part of the action easier to act on.

The CI row says ci.mjs 'reads no named secret', which is true. It could also note that ci.mjs passes the whole of process.env to the test process. Any secret present in the CI host environment would therefore reach the tests, even though none is granted or read.

The environments 'local build, CI' in section 2 come from inference (ci.mjs and the CI bar in feat.tasks). Cite file:ap_portal/ci.mjs and feat.tasks section 2 (CI bar) next to tool:repo-access for that column.
judge.notes:
I checked every statement against feat.tasks (TSK-06, TSK-07 and TSK-08 rows and notes), the tool view ('no secrets are required or granted for this repository'), and the ap_portal files the agent read this session: src/ap_portal/index.js, package.json, ci.mjs and tests/portal.test.js. They all match.

- index.js exports VERSION, LABELS, formatAmount and renderAgingSummary, with no require, network or env reads.
- package.json has no dependencies and a single 'ci' script.
- ci.mjs spreads process.env and adds NODE_PATH 'src'. It runs a syntax check, node --test with coverage, and static line checks.
- portal.test.js requires only node:test, node:assert and ap_portal, and uses literal values.

The previous refusal reason (portal.test.js cited without being read) is resolved: that file is now in the agent's read list and the claim about it is accurate. The TSK-07 helpers and constants, the files-in-budget list, 'CT-1 field list only (not TSK-06 code)', 'no transport layer… would re-trigger DES-01' and the synthetic SYN-INV-* feed owned by the Testing Agent are all quoted correctly from feat.tasks. FE-03 and FE-04 follow FE-02 as the SKILL.md says. The output holds no invented names, numbers or versions, and no secret values. The need/grant/gap analysis meets the outcome ('none needed, none granted, no request'). The only weak spot is the unsourced definition of what counts as a re-entry trigger, which is phrased as conditional process guidance; I list it under improvements rather than as a blocking hallucination.
